{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "hardware_incident",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "is_hardware_incident",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": false,
      "rationale": "This is a direct restatement of the focus variable hardware_incident itself, not an external associational variable. Grouping the focus against itself yields no informative relationship."
    },
    {
      "name": "incident_domain",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Well-separated, interpretable categories (hardware, software_application, database, network, vpn, etc.). However, it partially overlaps the focus since 'hardware' is one of its levels, making it somewhat circular; still, the non-hardware categories provide meaningful contrast for segmentation."
    },
    {
      "name": "hardware_failure_mode",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable failure-mode categories (not_functioning, connection_failure, not_powering_on, overheating, etc.) that are strongly associated with hardware. NULLs concentrate on non-hardware cases, so this segments the focus meaningfully, though it is largely defined only when hardware=true (near-tautological presence)."
    },
    {
      "name": "software_component_involved",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clear, human-readable software categories (database_client, os_update, vpn_client, office_suite). Its presence/NULL pattern is a good complementary signal that an incident is NOT hardware, supporting contrastive exploration."
    },
    {
      "name": "recurrence_signal",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "A clean binary (true/false) external attribute that can be cross-tabulated against hardware vs non-hardware incidents to explore whether recurrence associates with hardware problems."
    },
    {
      "name": "scope_context",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable spatial/scope categories (user_workstation, server_room, individual_device, building_wide) that can be segmented and compared against the focus to reveal where hardware incidents cluster."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 5,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.72,
  "rationale": "The set is largely strong for exploratory analysis: recurrence_signal, scope_context, software_component_involved, and the failure/domain columns provide interpretable, well-separated categories that a human can group and cross-tabulate against the hardware focus. Weaknesses: is_hardware_incident is a pure restatement of the focus and adds nothing, and incident_domain / hardware_failure_mode are partially circular (they contain 'hardware' as a level or are defined only for hardware cases), reducing genuine associational independence. Enough independent, interpretable segmentations remain to support meaningful relationship discovery, so informativeness is good but not maximal."
}
